text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today, extending a sharp two-week decline that intensified dramatically yesterday when the stock dropped nearly 4% in a single day. The sharp drop yesterday coincided with news that Saudi Arabia would release more crude oil into the market following a pipeline attack, which eased supply-disruption concerns — lower expected scarcity typically pressures oil majors' stock prices. Today's continued weakness reflects the same dynamic: oil prices remained flat on the day as markets priced in that the feared supply crunch from the Saudi pipeline outage was less severe than initially feared, removing upside support for energy stocks.

The broader backdrop adds weight to this near-term pressure. While geopolitical risks in the Middle East remain elevated (Saudi-Houthi clashes, U.S. involvement in the Iran conflict), signs of diplomatic progress toward a deal have emerged alongside the supply reassurance, suggesting the acute crisis premium is fading from the market. Diesel prices hitting records could support demand for fuel in coming weeks, but for now, the stock is reacting to the near-term relief in supply anxiety that was priced into energy stocks earlier this week.
